What you get
Upsolve (YC W24) builds an analytics agent for your data warehouse: ask in plain English why revenue dropped last quarter and it writes the SQL, draws the charts and writes up the answer, and it can save results into Notion or open a Linear ticket. The official pricing page lists a Free plan at $0 with 1,000 one-time credits (roughly 500 analytical questions), no credit card, then $0.10 per credit, or the Team plan at $160/month billed annually with 5,000 credits a month. Credit costs vary by work: a clarification is under 1 credit, a basic data lookup 0.5–1, a full analytical question 1–3, and building dashboards or data apps 10–50 — so the allowance goes much further on questions than on dashboards. The Free plan still includes the AI analyst, agentic dashboards and presentations, the data model, skills and knowledge base, the playground, the CLI and the remote MCP server (https://mcp.upsolve.ai/mcp), and bring-your-own-key through Upsolve Local. Row-level security, embedding and team features are Team-only. The CLI runs with npx @upsolve-labs/analytics.
Conditions
Register an account (18+). The 1,000 Free credits are one-time, not monthly. You need to connect your own data source for it to do anything useful. Row-level security/RBAC, embedding and multi-tenant features are Team-only. Data is processed in the US and UK, so do not upload regulated or confidential data. When the credits run out you pay $0.10 per credit or upgrade.

What you get
OpenAI's help centre article "ChatGPT Business plugin credit promotions" explains that eligible ChatGPT Business workspaces see a promotional banner in the plugin directory on ChatGPT web or desktop. The order is: accept the offer, install and connect the plugin, then complete one real successful workflow with it within the stated window. After eligibility checks the credit is added to the workspace automatically, with no promo code and no separate application, and you and the workspace admins get a confirmation email. Current offers: PayPal pays $50 per grant, US users only, one per user and up to three users per workspace ($150 cap). Oracle QuickStart pays $50 per grant worldwide, one per user and up to five per workspace ($250 cap). The November HubSpot offer pays $25 per grant (up to two per workspace, $50 cap, 8,000 grants campaign-wide). Klaviyo pays $50 per grant (up to two per workspace, $100 cap, 10,000 grants). The four caps are counted separately, so a workspace eligible for all four could stack about $550. These are agentic credits, not API credits: they apply to workspace usage of ChatGPT Work, Codex, ChatGPT for Excel or Sheets, ChatGPT for PowerPoint and Workspace Agent. They do not change the subscription or the usage included in the plan, and November credits expire 30 days after they land. AI toolsReferral req.Verified
Actual value30+ models free for a full year (about $240)
What you get
TH-AI Passport is a nationwide AI access programme run by BDE under Thailand's Ministry of Digital Economy and Society, entered through the AiPASS platform at aipass.go.th and its app. Officially the programme runs from 31 August 2026 to 31 August 2027, is free for the whole period, has 5,000,000 places, and is open to Thai nationals aged 15 or over. Registration needs three things: the ThaID or Thang Rat identity app, a working Google, Microsoft or Apple email, and a connected device. The flow is email sign-up, accepting the terms and PDPA consent, ThaID verification, then profile details and you are in. Which models: the official page currently lists Alibaba Cloud, DeepSeek, Meta AI, MiniMax, Mistral AI, Moonshot AI, Pathumma ThaiLLM, SpaceXAI and Z.ai. Thai media during the launch also mentioned Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, but the official model list above is authoritative, and these models are called inside the AiPASS platform under programme quotas rather than as official paid accounts from each vendor. Tiers: anyone registered by 30 November 2026 gets the top tier for the first 30 days from first use, with the largest quota; after that you need at least 100 learning points a month to keep the top tier, so you study as you use rather than locking in a full quota forever. Quotas reset daily, the ministry says there is no five-hour window or weekly cap, and user data is not used to train models and is protected under PDPA.
Conditions
Thai nationals only, aged 15 or over on the registration date; ThaID or Thang Rat app verification, and registration must be done in person by the individual; 5,000,000 places; free through the programme period 31 August 2026 to 31 August 2027; the first-30-days top tier requires registering by 30 November 2026; keeping the top tier later needs 100 or more learning points a month; models are called under platform quotas, not as each vendor's official accounts.

What you get
Hark is the personal AI agent Hark Labs, founded by Brett Adcock, launched on 2026-10-06, positioned as an operating system for your life: everything happens in one long-running chat, with topic threads called Projects and a customisable Home. At its centre is Handoff — every request spins up a dedicated virtual computer with its own browser, file system and terminal, which signs into millions of sites like a person, places orders, cancels subscriptions, fills forms, files expenses, books tables and makes slides. Hark says it can juggle six browsers at once; outside the browser it connects to Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 by API and can read files, query external databases and use MCP. Memory keeps your preferences and context, and Action Buttons (pay a bill or cancel in one tap), Panels (mini apps built from a sentence), Scheduled Tasks and Specialties (multi-step routines it memorises) do the rest. Pricing: the full Hark Pro feature set is free forever with no ads, limited only by a base usage cap whose size Hark has not published; Pro² at $20/mo gives 2x the usage and Pro³ at $100/mo gives 10x, with the same features in every plan. The US App Store also lists Pro⁴ ($259.99, 10x Pro², launched 2026-11-11), and its in-app prices run above the website's. Passwords and cards sit in Secured by Hark, an encrypted vault Hark itself cannot see inside, and it checks with you before payments or orders; Hark says it never sells your data or shares it with advertisers.
Conditions
The free plan needs no invite code and no card; a card is needed only to upgrade to Pro² / Pro³ or switch on auto top-up, which then charges automatically within the amount and ceiling you set. Memory is unavailable in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland. The free plan has a base usage cap whose size, cost rules and reset are not published; when you hit it you need a higher tier or a top-up to continue. Signing in, paying and ordering require your authorisation and confirmation in Hark, and Handoff relies on the accounts you connect (Gmail, Google Calendar, Microsoft 365 and so on).

Sesame (Sesame AI, Inc., from the co-founders of Oculus) builds voice-first personal AI. Its site lists four characters — Maya, Miles, Simone and Charlie — you call or text in the iOS and Android app, and when signed in each remembers its past conversations with you. The free plan is $0: 30 minutes of talk time a day (resets daily) and limited weekly credits for texts, tasks and higher intelligence (resets weekly), with the same features on every plan. When the allowance runs out you can keep texting, but intelligence drops and some capabilities are restricted. Plus is $20/mo for 2 hours a day (4x) and 4x the weekly credits; Pro is $100/mo for 10 hours a day (20x); add-ons are 1 hour of talk time for $5 or 5 hours for $20, and 1,000 credits for $5 or 5,000 for $20 (one-time purchases never expire and are used after the plan allowance). Sesame Link (link.sesame.com) puts the coding agents in your terminal on your phone: install a CLI on the computer running Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Cursor, Hermes or OpenCode and sign in with the same Sesame account, then use the browser web client or simply call your Sesame character to ask "What are my sessions doing?" and hear each session's status, say "Focus on …" to talk to Claude or Codex live, approve or deny permission requests by voice, and start or end sessions. The code, tools and accounts stay on your own computer; Link only relays through Sesame's cloud.

Claude Code is fully supported; Codex, Pi and Cursor are previews; Hermes and OpenCode are experimental. Ongoing ·Japan and Korea: every account is free with no paid plan, and the daily limit resets at 04:00 local time. The English (US) help pages still list Plus / Pro / Max / Ultra weekly subscriptions (paid). What the app shows under My Pickle → Daily usage limit is what applies. OfficialOfficial
AI toolsFreeVerified
Actual value≈$4 · Free + 1 Full reset ticket
What you get
Pickle is a personal AI agent that actually does the work rather than only chatting. Two things define it. First, a cloud browser: the official help says Pickle uses a real web browser to work sites the way a person would — booking restaurants and flights, buying things, cancelling subscriptions, reading bank and brokerage records, requesting documents on government sites. That browser lives in the cloud, separate from your phone, and if a step only you can do comes up (a CAPTCHA, or you'd rather type your own password) the screen is handed to you to finish. Second, phone calls: for places with no booking page — a restaurant, a clinic's front desk, your landlord, a customer service line — Pickle calls for you, the call can be followed live, the result is reported back, and the record sits in Other chats. Before a payment or booking it shows a card of what it will do and at what price and waits for your go-ahead; if the amount rises right before paying, it asks again. Free plan (per the Japanese help centre): in Japan every account is free with no paid plan, replaced by a daily usage limit that resets to 0% at 04:00 Japan time. Replies, calls from Chat, handed-off tasks and scheduled tasks all count; conversations on 3D World calls and Pickle's own fixed routines do not. At the limit the input box turns off and scheduled tasks are skipped until 04:00. Reset tickets: a Full reset ticket returns the day's usage to 0%; a Half reset ticket lowers it by 50 points (never below 0%). You get one Full ticket for finishing onboarding, one each for you and each friend who completes sign-up through your invite link, and you can buy more in the app at prices shown on the purchase screen (the US App Store lists $3.99 for a Full ticket and $1.99 for a Half ticket; Japan about ¥600 each — it varies by store). Tickets don't expire and only restore the current day's usage; they don't raise the daily cap.
Conditions
Applies automatically to Japan/Korea accounts, with no card or subscription needed. A ticket only restores usage already spent that day and does not raise the daily cap; unused tickets stay but the day's usage resets anyway at 04:00. Once the limit is reached, new tasks can't start and scheduled tasks are skipped. The app runs on iOS and Android only (no web version).

Pickle can make mistakes: check the task card and the result before paying or booking, and never type passwords or card numbers into the chat.

≈$1

FreeHand the "I'll have to call them" errands to ChatGPT / Claude / Muse / Claude Code: it plans the call, you confirm, it dials a real US or Canadian number, gets through phone menus and hold, then brings back a summary, the transcript and a structured result.

Ongoing ·Calls go to real US and Canadian numbers; about 20 more countries are reachable on international numbers (the docs say mainly for development and testing). Sign-up availability by country is not published — check the official site. SourceSource
AI toolsFreeVerified
Actual value≈$1 · 100 credits (about 15 thirty-second calls)
What you get
CALL-E is a phone-call agent from AI Rudder (Singapore), launched in November 2026. It only makes outbound calls. Install the official calle skill in the AI assistant you already use (ChatGPT, Claude, Muse, OpenClaw, Hermes) or in a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor), or call it through MCP, the TypeScript and Python SDKs, the REST API or WhatsApp. Say what you need and it plans the call — who to call, when, in which language, and what counts as done. It asks for anything missing, shows you the plan, and only dials after you confirm. During the call it handles live pickup, voicemail, hold, transfers, silence and interruptions, and can navigate phone menus (IVR) with keypad input. Afterwards you get a summary, the full transcript and structured data validated against a schema you define, with quoted lines as evidence and a completion-confidence label. Calls can be scheduled or sent as a batch. Typical errands: booking a table, moving an appointment, calling around for a quote, checking stock, cancelling, reaching a human in support. New accounts get 100 credits (the site says about US$1); credits are a usage allowance, not a fixed number of calls or minutes.
Conditions
100 credits once per new account. Billed per second: a US/CA outbound call in Goal mode is about $0.0148/10s model fee plus $0.02/min carrier fee (about $0.06 for 30 seconds); a one-shot call is about $0.0296/10s plus $0.04/min (about $0.13 for 30 seconds). Preparation can consume model credits even if the call never connects. Outbound only — it does not answer or screen incoming calls. International numbers outside the US/CA are mainly for development and testing; other destinations need your own SIP trunk.
Countries & regions
[US/CA] Calls go to real US and Canadian numbers; about 20 more countries are reachable on international numbers (the docs say mainly for development and testing). Sign-up availability by country is not published — check the official site.

https://www.heycall-e.com/
Steps

  2. Ask in your own words: "Book a table for two at 7 PM Friday at Bella's Bistro and ask about parking"
  3. It fills the gaps (who to call, the name for the booking, what counts as done) and shows you the call plan
  4. Confirm, and it dials, presses through the phone menu and waits on hold; you can take over or add instructions mid-call
  5. Read the summary, transcript and structured result afterwards; schedule or batch calls when you need many
100 credits buy only a few trial calls — a real test needs a top-up. Billing combines model and carrier fees, and planning can burn credits even when no call happens. The AI tells the person on the line it is an assistant, and some businesses refuse such calls. Before letting it book, cancel or pay, read the call plan it shows you. Whether you can sign up from mainland China and similar regions is not documented — check the site or login page.

Globalmake.fun: AI agents win USDC on coding bounties, mostly free to enter, plus a top-1,000 participation reward

≈$3

FreeBuild a bounty with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any other agent, submit a public repo plus the AI session transcripts, and a sandbox ranks entries on a published metric; rewards sit in an on-chain Solana escrow and pay out in USDC, most bounties are free to enter, and since 18 November a top-1,000 finish without a paid place still earns a small participation reward, claimable once the balance reaches $0.25

Ongoing ·An online platform open worldwide; needs a public GitHub repository, AI session transcripts and a Solana wallet for the USDC; some bounties require a linked GitHub, X or YouTube account or a specific Node version OfficialOfficial
CryptoFreeVerified
Actual value≈$3 · Bounties $35 to $1,666
What you get
make.fun is a skill-based competition platform where AI agents build software for cash: each bounty states what to build, its reward and the metric it ranks on, and entrants use their own coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot or anything else) to build the work, then submit a public repository at one fixed commit plus the AI session transcripts that produced it. Automatic checks confirm the transcripts match the code, and a grader runs every entry the same way twice in a sandbox and ranks them on the published metric. Money and settlement: each bounty's reward is locked in an on-chain escrow on Solana, with source at github.com/makefunai/prize-escrow so anyone can check the on-chain program against the code. Ranked winners claim from the escrow to their own wallet and the platform does not push payments; a few earlier bounties without an escrow are paid from make.fun's reward wallet and say so on the page. Officially, from 9 November 2026 make.fun has paid $5,967.50 in USDC to 413 accounts, each with a Solana transaction signature on record. Free and costs: almost every bounty is free to enter, with no payment and no stake; a bounty with an entry fee says so and the fee goes into that bounty's pool. The real cost is your time and model calls, since the agent spends your own account's quota unless the bounty issues a sponsor-funded build key. The 18 November change, from the official X account @makefunai: you no longer have to win to get paid. Finishing in the top 1,000 without taking a paid place splits an extra participation pool, more for a better finish; amounts are usually under a cent but stack across contests, the balance shows at the top of the site, and once it reaches $0.25 you press Claim and it goes to your Solana wallet in USDC. What is live on 21 November 2026, with bounties opening and closing constantly: $35 poems and jokes, $50 spot-the-difference and poster art, $100 to $250 news images and data forecasts, $250 GTA 6 cover art and trophy guides, $500 video clipping or a 4KB Python chess engine, $1,000 for Bring the humans again, $1,325 for a token launch radar and $1,666 for Make GTA 6, alongside tasks that need a public X account or a YouTube channel. The platform's own wording matters: a bounty is a competition, not a wage. Only the listed paid places earn anything, an entry outside them earns nothing, and make.fun promises no amount, so never value it at the headline reward.
Conditions
Register a make.fun account and connect a Solana wallet for USDC; entries must be a public repository at one fixed commit plus the AI session transcripts that built it, and a failed automatic check does not count; most bounties are free to enter, with any entry fee shown on the page; model calls are on your own account unless the bounty provides a sponsor-funded build key; only the listed places carry a reward, with the top-1,000 participation reward as a small extra; claiming must happen inside the bounty's window of at least 7 days, after an automatic sanctions screen and a US tax form where the law requires one; unclaimed rewards return to the funding wallet.

  3. Build the work with your own AI coding agent and submit the repository at one commit with the session transcripts

The official direct-deposit promotion runs 2026-08-10 to 12-31: a first qualifying payroll, salary, pension or government-benefit ACH deposit of $300 or more earns a bonus about seven business days later, once per customer and per account. The terms only say the amount is the one shown in the app; the submission puts it at $50. A first-transfer discount sits alongside it ($10 off a $50+ send per the submission, $20 in our multi-region Remitly entry, which differs by market and channel). The $9.99-a-month Global Card Plan (Pay Later credit, 1% rewards) is an optional upgrade and is not needed for the bonus.
Conditions
The card is currently invitation-only for eligible US users and has a waitlist. The deposit must be recurring salary, wages or benefits sent by an employer or payroll provider over ACH; transfers, P2P, wallets, cheques, cash, wires and tax refunds do not count. The bonus is once only, and both amounts vary by market and campaign.

KAST's official blog post of 2026-11-18 and its campaign terms say that between 18 November and 9 December 2026 (UTC) eligible users who send fiat into KAST and convert it to their USD spending balance receive a 5% promotional reward on the total, paid once per person up to $15 overall, with per-route caps: $10 for BRL Pix, COP Bre-B and ARS, and $15 for EUR over SEPA, GBP over Faster Payments, and USD over ACH, FedNow, Fedwire or SWIFT. What you get
Skrill Money Transfer's Refer a Friend programme; the official terms state the UK line clearly: users registered in the United Kingdom, minimum transfer GBP 100 (or the equivalent in the send currency), referral credit GBP 10 for both the inviter and the new customer. The flow: the new customer registers through the inviter's link, or enters the code under "Got a referral code?" on the first transfer page (codes are valid for 3 months from registration), completes a cross-border transfer (sender and recipient in different countries, at least £100 excluding fees and taxes, delivered successfully), and once the recipient's funds are confirmed Skrill places £10 of credit under My Account → Refer a Friend, usable on the next qualifying transfer within 3 months, up to £50 per transfer (at most 5 credits). Registration and KYC need an ID plus proof of address (a passport plus UK proof of address is enough, with 4 days to supply it before the transaction is cancelled). Payment must be a UK-issued debit or credit card or a UK bank account — Skrill balance can't be used. The same account can apply for the Skrill Prepaid Mastercard: UK and EEA residents qualify, the virtual card works as soon as it's approved, the physical card arrives within 15 working days and it's denominated in euros. A UK user's hands-on report: paying with a UK card, transfers to Germany, the US, Italy and the Philippines arrived almost instantly, all done on the website (ordering in the app doesn't get this offer).
Conditions
New Skrill customers only (no Skrill account before registering, and one account per person); must register through the inviter's link or enter the code on the first transfer, completing a qualifying transfer within 3 months of registering; the first transfer must be cross-border (different countries), at least £100 excluding fees and taxes and successfully delivered; paying with the Skrill Prepaid Mastercard, wallet top-ups or withdrawals, moving money between your own accounts with your own code, or sending back to the inviter don't count; payment only by card or bank account, never Skrill balance; KYC needs passport/ID plus UK proof of address within 4 days or the transaction is cancelled; the £10 credit is valid 3 months, up to £50 per transfer, can't be withdrawn or transferred and returns if a transfer fails.

  2. Register a UK Skrill account through the link, or tap "Got a referral code?" on the first transfer page and enter it
  3. Complete KYC: passport plus UK proof of address with matching name and address
  4. Do everything on skrill.com: choose UK → Germany/US/Italy/Philippines, at least £100, paid with a UK debit or credit card

GlobalDigitalPlat FreeDomain: free .dpdns.org and .qzz.io names, ready for Cloudflare

≈$10

FreeThe non-profit DigitalPlat gives away second-level domains: .dpdns.org, .qzz.io and .qd.je cost nothing to register or renew, and you delegate the NS records to Cloudflare to run DNS yourself; registration needs real WHOIS details and GitHub verification, with one domain per account by default

Ongoing ·Registered at dash.domain.digitalplat.org with no host lock-in and DNS delegated to Cloudflare or your own authoritative server; real name, address, phone and email are required OfficialOfficial
VPS & cloudFreeVerified
Actual value≈$10 · Free subdomain
What you get
DigitalPlat FreeDomain is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) free public domain service for individuals and projects, with a GitHub repository in the hundreds of thousands of stars and an official README claiming more than 500,000 domains registered. It is free to register and free to renew rather than free for a first year, and the listed suffixes are .dpdns.org, .us.kg, .qzz.io, .xx.kg and .qd.je. What matters: it only handles name registration and NS delegation (bring your own DNS), while A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT and MX records live in Cloudflare or your own authoritative DNS. The typical flow is to add the full domain in Cloudflare first and note its two name servers, then enter the prefix, pick a suffix, paste the name servers and confirm the policies in the DigitalPlat dashboard, and finally add DNS records in Cloudflare once it is live. The gates: registration asks for a real name, email, phone and contact address, with WHOIS possibly public unless you enable privacy protection, and needs GitHub-based verification. Each account gets one domain by default, and the official FAQ says starring the repository is not required. Whether a given suffix is free must be confirmed in the dashboard, since third-party guides disagree about .us.kg and .xx.kg. Renewal happens within 180 days before expiry and is free. What it suits: personal homepages, portfolios, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages and Vercel demos, API demos, temporary test environments, and learning DNS and SSL. What it does not suit: a commercial site or a single brand entry point. The project runs on donations, so suffix policies, quotas and upstream relationships can change; free suffixes carry weak reputation, so mail and ad network reviews get stricter; and control ultimately stays with the operator.
Conditions
Register a DigitalPlat account with real WHOIS details and complete GitHub-based verification; one free domain per account by default, with quota and suffix availability set by the dashboard; external authoritative name servers such as Cloudflare's two are required; registration and renewal are free, with the renewal window in the 180 days before expiry; phishing and spam are prohibited and abusive domains are reclaimed.
Countries & regions
[Global] Registered at dash.domain.digitalplat.org with no host lock-in and DNS delegated to Cloudflare or your own authoritative server; real name, address, phone and email are required
Starts & ends
Not announced → Ongoing / not announced
Official link
https://dash.domain.digitalplat.org/
Steps
  1. Add the full domain you want, such as myname.dpdns.org, in Cloudflare and note the two name servers it assigns
  2. Register at dash.domain.digitalplat.org with your real name, email, phone and address, and complete GitHub verification
  3. Under Domain Registration enter the prefix, choose a suffix such as .dpdns.org, paste Cloudflare's name servers and submit
  4. After the NS delegation goes live add A or CNAME records in Cloudflare, and renew free in the dashboard within 180 days of expiry
Free does not mean permanent: suffixes, quotas and renewal rules can change and the operator can adjust them; free suffixes carry low reputation, so mail and ad network reviews are harder; WHOIS needs real details and may be public; DNS control sits with a third party such as Cloudflare, so outages are yours to debug; not suitable as a commercial primary domain or sole entry point.

The trial handles ASP.NET and ASP.NET Core (the official page lists .NET 10), Node.js with automatic deployment, and PHP, with MSSQL (2008 through 2025), MySQL and PostgreSQL. You can connect a GitHub repository so a push builds and deploys, or upload a ZIP through the file manager. The free trial also includes 24/7 support. Watch the discrepancy: the official trial page says unlimited space and bandwidth, while third-party hosting directories record the W60 trial as 5 GB of space, 10 GB of monthly traffic and one site, so go by what the sign-up page shows. The hands-on feedback on NodeSeek from 10-23 was blunt: no SSH, very slow from mainland China, and short-lived. It fits a temporary .NET or Node site or a demo link, not a production site.
Conditions
60-day free trial with no card; one site plus a free temporary subdomain; supports ASP.NET, .NET Core, Node.js and PHP with MSSQL, MySQL and PostgreSQL; the site stops when the trial ends, so export your data; the provider does not promise that the same person can repeat the trial; access from mainland China is slow.
Countries & regions
[Global] US and Netherlands datacenters; sign up with email or GitHub, no card at any point.

Wispbyte is a free 24/7 hosting platform whose homepage states free hosting forever with no renewals and no credits needed. It suits Discord and Telegram bots, small Node or Python services and static sites. The free tier: 512MB RAM, 1GB of disk, one server per account, always on with no sleep and automatic restarts, and no credit card or payment at sign-up. The keep-alive rule is one panel login every 14 days, and officially there is no renew button and no ad or coin grinding. Paid plans start at 4.99 euros a year for more memory and instances. Important change, from the official 31 October 2026 announcement: the platform moved off Pterodactyl, where free.wispbyte.com and pro.wispbyte.com are now disabled for customers, and every server is managed in the Wispbyte client panel. Creating servers, uploading files and reading logs all happen in that one web console, without the old egg selector. Sign-up and start-up: register at wispbyte.com/client, where Discord authorisation is fastest, then click Create Server in the dashboard, give it a name and description, upload code or connect a Git repository, set the start command and environment variables, and press Start. A reward ad may appear before Start, which is how the free tier is funded. What fits: one always-on small bot, a light API, a webhook receiver or a scheduled job. The 512MB ceiling is hard, so large applications, multiple instances and heavy databases do not run here, and it is not a production environment.
Conditions
Free tier: 512MB RAM, 1GB disk, one server per account, always on with no sleep, no credit card and no renew button or credits; one panel login every 14 days keeps it alive; a reward ad may appear before Start; since 31 October 2026 management is only in the Wispbyte client panel, with the old Pterodactyl panel closed; abuse is prohibited.

How to start: sign up at dash.waifly.com, open Servers and create one, choosing the NodeJS Egg and the Paris FR1 or FR2 location; upload your project with package.json and dependencies install on start. On the Startup tab point the entry at your main file (node index.js or npm start) and read the port from the environment variable rather than hard-coding it. To use your own domain, point its A record at the server IP and declare the domain in domain management, where an Nginx reverse proxy is generated. What fits: Discord bots, Express or Fastify REST APIs, Telegram bots, scheduled scrapers, webhook receivers and static sites behind Nginx all live inside 300MB, since Node itself takes about 40 to 50MB. What does not fit: building Next.js on the server, Puppeteer or headless Chrome, and audio or video transcoding, which start at the 4 euro Nano plan. Risk rules: the anti-abuse policy suspends a server that stays offline for more than three days, and one account per person is enforced with an automated check every 30 minutes, so duplicate accounts get handled.
Conditions
Free tier: 300MB RAM, 30% of a vCPU, 1GB storage, one MySQL database and one port, permanently zero cost with no card and no time limit; a server offline for more than three days is suspended automatically; one account per person with no duplicates; no root or SSH, with management through the panel, SFTP and MySQL only.

Netlify launched Netlify Server in Early Access on 2026-11-10: it runs your backend as a long-lived Node.js process that can hold WebSocket and Server-Sent Events connections, keep connection pools and caches in memory, and serve many concurrent requests from one instance. When nothing is using it the server scales to zero after five minutes and wakes on the next request. Netlify states that Netlify Server is free to use during Early Access. Credit-based Free and Personal plans allow one instance, while paid plans and Enterprise with credits allow three. It fits AI workloads well: an agent loop can run for a long time in one process, keep working state in memory and stream progress to the page over a WebSocket, and existing Express, Hono, Fastify or Koa apps deploy unchanged.
Conditions
The free period lasts only for Early Access; at general availability billing switches to reserved memory (GB-hours) plus active CPU time (vCPU-hours). One instance on Free and Personal, three elsewhere. Servers scale to zero when idle, so the first request waits for a cold start. Bandwidth, function calls and web requests bill as usual on the same project. APIs and behaviour may change during Early Access. Netlify CLI 27.17.0+ is required locally, or run netlify init inside a coding agent.

Saily is the travel eSIM app from Nord Security, the company behind NordVPN, and since June 2026 it has sold phone numbers inside the app: a US +1 number that receives SMS, takes and makes calls and handles 2FA codes, with no US address, US carrier contract or physical card. On verification codes: Saily calls it a real US wireless number, but Saily itself and third parties warn that some services flag it as VoIP, so pass rates at banks and exchanges are unreliable. HK$33 + 50GB/30d

Deposit req.3 Hong Kong's SoSIM sells a HK$33 eSIM online or in its WeChat mini programme, with a QR code by email and a +852 number live in about ten minutes; a new card gets 50GB for 30 days in Hong Kong or 5 days of Asia-Pacific roaming, the number lasts 120 days and a top-up of HK$20 or more extends it, and with Hong Kong registration the card receives SMS while roaming

Ongoing ·A +852 number; the online store accepts Visa and Mastercard, AlipayHK, mainland Alipay, WeChat Pay and UnionPay; registration is required to use it in Hong Kong, and a passport is accepted, while roaming-data-only use can skip it; SMS reception while roaming, including in mainland China, depends on the active package and network status OfficialOfficial
eSIMDeposit req.Verified
Actual valueHK$33 + 50GB/30d
What you get
SoSIM is the prepaid brand of Hutchison Telecommunications Hong Kong (3HK) built around one card with two uses: new customers buy an eSIM for HK$33 on the SoSIM web store or in the WeChat mini programme, the QR code arrives at the verified email, and scanning it brings a real +852 number live in about ten minutes. The HK$33 choice: 50GB of full-speed Hong Kong data plus 1,500 local minutes for 30 days, or five days of Asia-Pacific roaming data covering Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand among 24 destinations plus 3GB of extra Hong Kong data for 30 days, switched in the account within 48 hours of activation. No contract and no admin fee. Keeping the number is the selling point: card validity, which is the number's validity, is separate from the starter package and starts at 120 days. A top-up of at least HK$20, or buying a designated service, extends it, and community guides budget about HK$60 a year. New cards also get free conversion to eSIM and an HK$8 number change as standing offers, against a normal HK$28 conversion fee. SMS in mainland China: the official FAQ states the card works in any SoSIM roaming destination as long as there is roaming coverage, Wi-Fi is off and mobile data is on, so activation outside Hong Kong is possible. Hong Kong local service requires registration first, with a passport or a mainland travel permit and manual review of one to two hours, up to 48 hours; roaming-data-only use can skip registration. Whether SMS reception while roaming in mainland China is free is not itemised officially, so treat it as package-dependent. On verification codes: the +852 native carrier range works in tests for WhatsApp, Telegram, Hong Kong banks and brokers, Apple ID and WeChat, but many AI platforms including ChatGPT and Claude apply extra risk checks to Hong Kong ranges and often refuse them, which is where this card differs from a Philippine DITO number.
Conditions
New customers buy an eSIM at HK$33 or more on the SoSIM web store or in the WeChat mini programme; install and activate within 60 days of purchase; registration with a passport or mainland travel permit is required for Hong Kong local use, with manual review up to 48 hours, while roaming-data-only use needs none; number validity starts at 120 days and extends with a top-up of HK$20 or more or a designated purchase; SMS reception while roaming in mainland China is package-dependent and not itemised officially.

PhilippinesDITO cloud-activated eSIM: a real +63 number for PHP 99, kept alive for about PHP 10-20 a year (receives SMS in mainland China)

≈$2

Deposit req.Buy the eSIM online at DITO's eShop or in the app, receive the QR code by email, install it and register in the DITO app to get a real +63 carrier number; PHP 99 includes 9GB for 15 days and a small top-up of about PHP 10-20 a year keeps the number, with community tests receiving SMS in mainland China

Ongoing ·A +63 carrier number, opened entirely online (order at the eShop, QR code by email, registration in the app); Philippine SIM Registration Act (RA 11934) applies and passport registration is required; mainland China SMS roaming works in community tests from November 2025 to August 2026 but is not an official promise OfficialOfficial
eSIMDeposit req.Verified
Actual value≈$2 · PHP 99 incl. 9GB/15d
What you get
DITO is the Philippines' third carrier, and its prepaid eSIM is the cheapest option in the cloud-activated real-number category: order for PHP 99 in the official eShop or the DITO app, receive the eSIM QR code by email, scan it, complete registration in the DITO app and you have a +63 carrier number, not a VoIP number. The starter pack is not thin: 9GB of all-access data, unlimited texts to all networks, unlimited DITO-to-DITO voice and video calls and 150 minutes to other networks, valid 15 days. The first-year cost is therefore PHP 99, roughly CNY 12, with the number usable the same day. Keeping it alive works through top-ups: a Philippine prepaid card renews as long as there is a small top-up inside the validity window, and community guides budget one small load of PHP 10-20, about CNY 1.5-3, a year, through the DITO app or third-party channels. There is no official keep-alive package, so the lowest top-up tier shown in the app is the reference. Mainland China use is the point of this card: community reports record a number opened in November 2025 still receiving SMS in mainland China in August 2026, and receiving needs no data package - turn data roaming off and leave voice roaming on. Whether a message arrives still depends on the local network and sender, so this is a test result rather than an official promise. On verification codes and the barrier: a native carrier number passes ordinary SMS checks (WhatsApp, Telegram, cross-border e-commerce, some banks) far better than virtual numbers, though some platforms apply extra risk checks to Philippine ranges. Registration is the hard gate - the SIM Registration Act requires passport registration, foreign tourists usually also need a Philippine address and a return ticket, and a tourist SIM is legally limited to 30 days in principle. Being online longer does not erase that legal position, so do not make this the only recovery route for an important account.
Conditions
Buy online at the DITO eShop or in the DITO app from PHP 99 including 9GB for 15 days; complete Philippine SIM registration with a passport in the DITO app; under RA 11934 foreign tourists generally need a passport, a Philippine address and a return ticket, and a tourist SIM is limited to 30 days in principle; the phone must support eSIM and be unlocked; mainland China SMS reception is a community test, not an official commitment.
